items.headline: Sysdig confirms first in-the-wild exploitation of the 9.9 Langflow IDOR (CVE-2026-55255)
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's security item was a cluster of critical RCE CVEs in agentic-AI developer tooling, framed as disclosed-but-abstract: Flowise's 9.9 custom-MCP command injection at the center, with Crawl4AI, Langflow and picklescan scoring 9.6-9.8 in the same late-June window, plus a Mastra flaw reportedly touched by Lazarus and a LiteLLM entry on CISA's KEV list. Langflow appeared there only as one 9.x name in the list. Today sharpens that thread into a confirmed incident: Sysdig reports the first observed active exploitation of CVE-2026-55255, a CVSS 9.9 IDOR in Langflow that lets an authenticated user run flows across tenant boundaries, fixed in 1.9.2. The fresh angle beyond yesterday's disclosure framing is twofold — this is now a first-seen in-the-wild exploitation rather than a theoretical advisory, and Sysdig makes the explicit point that raw CVSS poorly predicts which flaws actually get exploited, shifting the story from severity scoring to observed attacker behavior at the same MCP/tool-execution boundary flagged yesterday.

items.headline: Unsloth v0.1.471-beta ships GLM 5.2 support, ~3x longer auto-fit context and Blackwell RTX
items.diff_narrative: No Unsloth item appeared on yesterday's slate; the project had been searched but left unbulleted on 07-01, so it returns to the bullet set today with a concrete release. Unsloth v0.1.471-beta adds day-of support for GLM 5.2, roughly 3x longer context via automatic memory auto-fit, and Blackwell RTX support, alongside a redesigned model Hub and a new --secure flag for the training/inference workflow. This is a distinct thread from anything on yesterday's slate, which was dominated by Anthropic's Sonnet 5 and Claude Science releases; today's open-tooling angle is local fine-tuning and long-context efficiency on consumer Blackwell silicon, with the --secure flag quietly echoing the same tool-execution-safety concern running through today's Langflow item.

items.headline: Mistral 3 open-weight family lands: Large 3 MoE plus dense 14B/8B/3B under Apache 2.0
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday carried no Mistral or open-weight model-release item — its model news was entirely Anthropic's Sonnet 5 (a proprietary, API-priced mid-tier agent) and the non-model Claude Science harness. Today adds a fully open counterweight: the Mistral 3 family, released under Apache 2.0, led by Mistral Large 3, a mixture-of-experts model with 41B active of 675B total parameters, and rounded out by dense 14B, 8B and 3B variants. The models are pitched as agentic, which puts an openly licensed option directly alongside the closed agent-model story from yesterday and extends the week's agent thread from harnesses and hardware into the open-weights column.

items.headline: AMD confirms Advancing AI 2026 for July 22-23 with MI400, Helios and a memory-led framing
items.diff_narrative: Hardware had no dedicated bullet yesterday, where AMD's Advancing AI appeared only as a carried date inside the events tracker (July 22-23). Today promotes it to a story of its own: AMD confirms the July 22-23 event and previews the MI400 accelerator on CDNA 5 at 2nm, the Helios rack-scale system, and greater than 2x the memory bandwidth of MI350, explicitly framing the next cycle as memory-led with HBM sold out through 2026. That memory-led framing ties loosely back to the Micron HBM supply thread from 06-29 — where Micron's high-bandwidth-memory capacity was the earlier data point, AMD now casts memory bandwidth and HBM scarcity as the gating factor for the accelerator generation itself, connecting the supply-side signal to a named product roadmap.

items.headline: AI events calendar refresh — World's Fair closes today, chip and security dates carried
items.diff_narrative: The events tracker carries over from yesterday but advances the AI Engineer World's Fair from its final-stretch framing to its actual close: where yesterday placed it in its last two days running through July 2 with the Harness Engineering keynote closing it out, today marks World's Fair as closing today. The forward calendar is otherwise carried intact across the three sub-tracks — AMD Advancing AI (now surfaced as its own story) on July 22-23, Hot Chips on August 23-25, and the AI Infra Summit on September 15-17, with the security block clustered early-to-mid August. The attendance-planner framing continues to tie to the agent-tooling-CVE thread, now anchored by today's confirmed Langflow exploitation, and to the secure-AI-accelerator watch reinforced by AMD's memory-led hardware preview.
